partners.diseaseBName: thrombophilia due to protein C deficiency, autosomal dominant
partners.mechanism_chain: ANO5 (HGNC:27481) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D metabolism (GO:0006629); Vitamin D metabolism (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia (MONDO:0008151); PROC (HGNC:9109) —DISRUPTS→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-60141); Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-60141) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombophilia due to protein C deficiency, autosomal dominant (MONDO:0008316); Vitamin D metabolism (GO:0006629) —INCREASES→ Coagulation cascade (REACT:R-HSA-60141). Loss-of-function mutations in ANO5 disrupt vitamin D metabolism, contributing to gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia. Protein C (encoded by PROC) is a vitamin K-dependent protein involved in the coagulation cascade. Vitamin K is essential for the gamma-carboxylation of Gla residues in vitamin K-dependent proteins, including protein C. Impaired vitamin D metabolism can indirectly affect vitamin K availability or utilization, thereby impacting protein C function and leading to thrombophilia. Thus, disruptions in vitamin D metabolism (affected by ANO5) can converge on and exacerbate defects in the coagulation cascade (affected by PROC).
